applicant_utility.summary: Every international fee-paying student Waterloo admits to a full-time first-year degree program automatically receives $10,000, credited as $5,000 against each of the first two terms' tuition bills - there is no form, essay, GPA floor, or competitive cap. The real contest is admission itself, so the practical deadlines are the OUAC application cutoffs (January 15 for Engineering, February 1 for everything else) for a September start. Because the money is locked to tuition, treat it as a discount on first-year fees, not as spending money for rent or flights.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International fee-paying students holding an offer to a standard first-year Waterloo degree program who want a guaranteed tuition offset with zero extra paperwork.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply through OUAC in time for the September 2027 entry cycle: January 15, 2027 for Engineering (other than Architecture), February 1, 2027 for other programs
Get transcripts and any required English test scores in by the matching document deadline (February 1 / February 15, 2027)
Confirm your program is not excluded (Social Work, Optometry, Pharmacy, Medical Sciences/Medicine, 2+2-style programs) and that you are not entering with transfer credits
From mid-April, monitor the Awards and financial aid tab in the Waterloo applicant portal for the award posting
Budget the remaining first-year costs - residence, meals, study permit, flights - before accepting the offer
common_rejection_risks: Entering as a transfer student with transfer credits, which voids scholarship eligibility entirely
Switching to non-international fee status before or during the term and losing the remaining installment
Dropping below three courses in either first or second term (no longer full-time) and forfeiting the installment
Applying to an excluded program - Bachelor of Social Work, Doctor of Optometry, Doctor of Pharmacy, Medical Sciences/Doctor of Medicine
Deferring an offer carried over from a previous admission year, which the exclusions list rules out even though deferring a current offer does not
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, residence and meal plans, travel to Canada, study permit and biometrics fees, and all tuition beyond the first year - the $10,000 is credited to tuition bills only and cannot be paid out as cash.
document_audit: The scholarship requires no documents and no bank information - any request for payment or account details to 'release' the funds is not from Waterloo
If claiming the English-school exemption, official transcripts showing language of instruction or a principal's letter must arrive by the document deadline, and emailed letters are not accepted

English test scores must be sent by the testing agency directly to Waterloo (TOEFL institution code 0996, department code 00), and your name, email, and date of birth must match your OUAC application or scores will not link automatically
alerts: The award is not cash: $5,000 posts toward the first-term bill in late July and $5,000 toward the second-term bill in late November only
You must remain registered full-time (three or more courses) and remain an international fee-paying student in both terms to keep each installment

The FAQ deferral answers are inconsistent - the exclusions list bars students who deferred an admission from a previous year while the FAQ says deferring your offer is fine; confirm with Waterloo before deferring
First-year admission at Waterloo is for the September-start term only, so a missed cycle costs a full year of scholarship eligibility
The award stacks with other Waterloo entrance scholarships (President's, Merit) and does not reduce them
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: OUAC application for September entry -> offer of admission -> automatic scholarship posting on the Awards and financial aid tab in the applicant portal from mid-April -> $5,000 tuition credits applied in late July and late November.

official.deadline_note: If December 1 falls on a weekend or a federal holiday, applications must be submitted by the following business day before 8:00 p.m. (ET). Applicants must also respect each institution's internal deadline for admission to the intended program - contact the faculty of graduate studies.

benefits: Supports up to 3,298 students annually in all disciplines
Apply to up to three institutions using the Research Portal; selection and post-award administration are carried out at the institutional level

Associated supplements and joint initiatives include the Department of National Defence MINDS Scholarship Initiative, the Indigenous Scholars Awards and Supplements Pilot Initiative, and the Canada Research Training Awards Suite - Research Travel Supplements

Indigenous Scholars Supplement valued at $5,000 for successful CGRS M applicants (to the limit of available funding); alternate-list Indigenous students may receive a $27,000 Indigenous Scholars Award plus the $5,000 supplement
Each agency has up to 20 additional CGRS M awards reserved for Black student researchers, for applicants who self-identify and consent
eligibility: Be a Canadian citizen, a permanent resident of Canada, or a Protected Person under subsection 95(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (Canada) as of the application deadline date

Be registered in, have applied for, or will apply for admission to an eligible graduate program at the master's or doctoral level that can be started within the eligible dates of the competition year at a Canadian institution with a CGRS M allocation
Respect the internal deadline to apply for admission for the intended program of study at the selected institution

Have completed between 0 and 12 months of full-time study (or equivalent) in the program for which funding is requested as of December 31 of the year of application (or between 4 and 12 months in the specified fast-track case)
Not have held or be currently holding a Master's-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC
Not have held or be currently holding an Indigenous Scholars Award and/or Supplement
Have achieved a first-class average as determined by the host institution(s) in each of the last two completed years of study (institutions may accept applications without this at their discretion)
Apply to only one CRTAS program per academic year through CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC - only the first eligible application is retained

Program must be predominantly research oriented (thesis, major research project, dissertation, scholarly publication, performance, recital and/or exhibit); course-work-only master's programs are typically not eligible
requirements: Complete application submitted by the deadline using the Research Portal, following all 11 steps in the instructions for completing an application
Submit the application to the institution(s) at which you intend to hold the award
Applications may be submitted in either English or French; supporting documents in other languages require a certified translation
Joint programs with a professional degree and clinically oriented programs are eligible only with a significant autonomous research component
documents: Complete application submitted through the Research Portal, prepared according to the published instructions for completing an application (all 11 steps)
Certified translations of any supporting documents written in a language other than English or French
selection_criteria: Academic excellence - 50% (academic record, scholarships and awards held, duration of previous studies, type of program and courses pursued, relative standing)

Research potential - 30% (quality and originality of contributions, relevance of experience and training, significance, feasibility and merit of proposed research, judgment and critical thinking, initiative and autonomy)
Personal characteristics and interpersonal skills - 20% (work and leadership experience, project management, communication of concepts, involvement in academic life, volunteerism)
Merit review is carried out by institutions with an allocation, coordinated by the faculty of graduate studies
coverage: $27,000 scholarship for 12 months (published value and duration)
Research travel is funded separately through the Canada Research Training Awards Suite - Research Travel Supplements competition, not through the core award
application_method: Complete and submit an application to up to three institutions using the Research Portal
Follow all 11 steps in the Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Master's program: Instructions for completing an application before the portal closes
Contact the faculty of graduate studies at each intended institution for internal admission deadlines and subject-matter guidance
official.application_route: Submit one application through the tri-agency Research Portal to up to three Canadian institutions by December 1, 8:00 p.m. ET; institutional committees conduct the merit review.
official.study_mode: full-time; part-time support details are set out in the Tri-agency research training award holder's guide
official.citizenship_residency: Canadian citizen, permanent resident of Canada, or Protected Person under subsection 95(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act as of the application deadline date.
official.international_eligibility: No - eligibility explicitly requires Canadian citizenship, permanent residence, or Protected Person status as of the application deadline date.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Apply through the agency matching your field of research (CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC); the host institution must have a CGRS M allocation for that field, and applications deemed mislabelled will be re-labelled per agency subject-matter guidelines.
official.research_requirement: Yes - the program must be predominantly research oriented, leading to a thesis, major research project, dissertation, scholarly publication, performance, recital and/or exhibit; course-work-only programs are typically ineligible, and acceptance into a major research component stream must be confirmed before holding the award.
official.description: The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Master's program provides financial support to high-calibre scholars engaged in an eligible master's or, in some cases, doctoral program in Canada, allowing them to concentrate more fully on their studies in their chosen fields.
official.program_type: Federal research training scholarship (Canada Research Training Awards Suite, administered by CIHR, NSERC, and SSHRC)
official.english_requirement: No English or French proficiency test score is specified for the scholarship; applications may be submitted in either of Canada's official languages, and documents in other languages require certified translations.

applicant_utility.summary: CGRS-M pays $27,000 for one year of research-based master's (or direct-entry/fast-track doctoral) study, but only Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and Protected Persons as of the deadline can hold it - international students are excluded outright. You file one application through the tri-agency Research Portal to up to three institutions, and the December 1 federal cutoff hides a harder constraint: each institution's own internal deadline, which is often weeks earlier. Scoring is transcript-heavy (academic excellence 50%, research potential 30%), so grades and a feasible, well-argued proposal matter more than extracurricular breadth.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving Canadian and permanent-resident students entering a thesis-based master's or direct-entry doctorate who can secure a supervisor and clear institutional deadlines before December.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you will be within 0 to 12 months of study in the program as of December 31 of the application year, and that you hold no previous master's-level tri-agency scholarship
Shortlist up to three institutions that hold a CGRS M allocation in your field and clear each one's internal admission deadline, not just the December 1 federal date
Verify your program is research-based (thesis or equivalent) and, where required, secure confirmed acceptance into the major research component stream
Choose the correct agency for your field before applying - mislabelled applications are re-labelled against subject-matter guidelines and can land at an institution without an allocation
Work through all 11 portal steps well before December 1, 8:00 p.m. ET, to avoid peak-season portal congestion
common_rejection_risks: Applying to more than one CRTAS program in the same year - only the first eligible application is retained
Meeting the federal December 1 deadline but missing a host institution's earlier internal cutoff
Course-work-only or clinically oriented programs without a significant autonomous research component
Falling outside the 0-12 month study window (or the 4-12 month fast-track case) as measured on December 31
Holding another tri-agency award, which cannot be held concurrently with CGRS M (the Research Travel Supplements are the only exception)
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and most living expenses in high-cost cities remain the student's responsibility; research travel is only covered if you separately win a CRTAS Research Travel Supplement.
document_audit: Supporting documents outside English or French need certified translations - budget time for this before the portal deadline
Your identity details must be consistent across the Research Portal, transcripts, and each institution's admission file, or the application cannot be linked
Selection is coordinated by the faculty of graduate studies, so confirm directly with the institution that your file is complete rather than assuming the federal portal covers it
alerts: Late applications are never accepted, and the agencies explicitly warn that portal delays near the deadline can block submission - submit days early
Results post in the Research Portal from April 1 and alternate offers can continue until January 31; checking the portal is your responsibility
International students are not eligible - do not spend the cycle preparing if you are not a citizen, permanent resident, or Protected Person as of the deadline

Indigenous applicants must select the Indigenous Scholars Awards and Supplements Pilot Initiative option in the Supplements/Joint Initiatives section of the form, and documentation under the Tri-agency Policy on Indigenous Citizenship and Membership Affirmation is required if successful
Awards are tenable only at the institution where the offer originates and moving tenure later requires host institution and agency approval
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Research Portal application (11 steps) to up to three institutions by December 1, 8:00 p.m. ET -> institutional merit review by allocation holders (50/30/20 criteria) -> offers visible in the portal from April 1, alternates through January 31.
